title: Squeezing for dispersive readout of NV magnetometer
authors: A. M. Kozodaev, S. M. Drofa, P. G. Vilyuzhanina, A. Chernyavskiy, N. I. Salangin, A. N. Smolyaninov, S. Ya. Kilin, I. S. Cojocaru, S. V. Bolshedvorskii, V. V. Soshenko, F. Y. Khalili, A. V. Akimov
abstract: Nitrogen vacancy centers in diamond have established themselves as good sensing element for various type of sensors. In particular magnetometers based on diamond impurities are quickly developing and are already on the market. Yet, optical readout in these systems complicates system design. Recently schemes of dispersive readout of nitrogen vacancy spin state using high finesse dielectric cavities for microwave field were proposed, which do not use the optical readout scheme. However, only shot noise based estimates were so far done for sensitivity of these devices. Here we provide detailed analysis of various practically relevant noise and loss sources for such a system. Furthermore, we consider the possibility of using the squeezing quantum state of the probing microwave field and show it allows to improve the device performance even at room temperature.
summary: The paper theoretically analyzes the noise limitations of microwave dispersive readout magnetometers based on NV centers. By incorporating quantum squeezing into the probing field, the authors derive methods to suppress measurement noise below the standard shot-noise limit. This demonstrates a pathway to significantly enhance magnetometer sensitivity even under realistic room-temperature operating conditions.
main_problem: To improve the sensitivity of Nitrogen Vacancy (NV) magnetometer readout by utilizing quantum squeezing in the probing microwave field, especially for dispersive readout schemes that avoid optical detection.
main_result: Squeezing the input microwave field allows for a reduction in the minimum total noise spectral density below the standard shot-noise limit, improving device performance even at room temperature.
method: The analysis uses quantum Langevin equations solved in the frequency domain to derive the output field operator and subsequently calculate the noise spectral density by optimizing detection angles.
model_or_system: The system involves NV centers (modeled as an effective Two-Level System) coupled dispersively to a microwave cavity. The dynamics are governed by linearized Langevin equations incorporating input, loss, and spin noise sources.
key_observables: Noise spectral density $S_\delta(\Omega)$, minimum detectable magnetic field ($\eta$), and the output homodyne signal $\hat{b}_\psi^{	ext{out}}(\Omega)$.
important_parameters: Cavity quality factor ($Q$), input power ($P_{	ext{in}}$), effective coupling rate ($g_{eff}$), and squeezing angle ($	heta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Markov approximation, linearization of Langevin equations, and assumes negligible interaction between different NV centers for initial derivations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the experimental scheme and input/output quantum noise components; Figure 1(f) shows how the output field can be squeezed.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the Hamiltonian and Langevin equations to solving them in the frequency domain, deriving the full output field expression, calculating the noise spectral density by optimizing detection angles ($	heta$ and $\psi$), and finally analyzing the scaling of sensitivity with NV concentration and cavity parameters.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed quantum noise analysis for solid-state magnetometry, directly applying advanced concepts like squeezing to overcome fundamental measurement limits in a highly relevant platform (NV centers).

NV sensing of materials.note: This paper directly analyzes the sensitivity enhancement ($\eta$) of an NV magnetometer using quantum techniques (squeezing) for magnetic field detection, which is central to the theme of spin-defect sensing of magnetic properties.
